text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Diabetic Bullae (Eruptive Bullous Diabetes)

I see you are a 65-year-old with well-controlled diabetes and regular sun exposure. Given your history, the sudden appearance of bullae on the hand without typical signs of infection or trauma is highly suggestive of eruptive bullous diabetes. Do you recall if these blisters appeared spontaneously on intact skin?
